answer: Escrowed Reputation Handoff. An identity's standing sits in a crystal ledger that only transfers after a full audit trail clears, so a fresh clone starts at zero and cannot inherit its parent's history. Each new key must post a velvet deposit locked for a fixed audit window, and that deposit is forfeited to the auditor pool the moment duplicate behaviour surfaces. Because the deposit exceeds any reward a clone can earn before detection, the marginal clone is strictly negative-EV, and attackers pay that basalt-hard floor per identity every time they spin up a copy.
